etymologies.etymologyHTML: From Latin diārium (“a daily allowance for soldiers, in Late Latin also ‘diary’”), neuter of *diārius, from diēs (“a day”) (whence also journal). Cognate with Spanish diario (“daily; diary”).

definitions.definition: A daily log of experiences, especially those of the writer.

quote.citation: 2005 January 30, Jef Biederman, “Feng Shui Is Like So Passe”, in Totally Spies!: Undercover, season 3, episode 19, spoken by Alexandra “Alex” (Andrea Baker as Clover and Katie Griffin), Marathon Media, via Teletoon:
quote.text: No, I’m just going over the stuff Tara wrote in my diary.She’s writing your diary? Could you be any lazier?

definitions.definition: (British, Canada) A personal organizer or appointment diary.

quote.text: It is recommended that teachers and pupils are issued with homework diaries to help implement and monitor the homework timetable.

definitions.definition: (intransitive) To keep a diary or journal.

quote.text: As part of her mindful movement practise, diarying is important to Sarah. "It gives me a chance to see what is going on, to reflect on my experience."

quote.citation: 1605, Francis Bacon, a letter to the Lord Chancellor, touching the History of Britain:
quote.text: the offer of a usurpation, though it were but as a diary ague
